title: Yellow Flaky American Corn Flatbread
description: A briny and flaky American dish featuring celery salt and a ferment, this corn flatbread is perfect for showing off, and is shojin-friendly to boot, made with a natural yeast starter and free from animal products.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, and celery salt, whisking to incorporate.
Add the natural yeast starter, water, and olive oil to the dry ingredients, stirring with a wooden spoon until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10 minutes, until the dough becomes smooth and elastic.
Form the dough into a ball, place it in a lightly oiled bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees, with a baking stone inside, if available.
Punch down the dough, divide it into 6 equal pieces, and roll each piece into a thin circle.
Place the dough circles on the preheated baking stone, if using, or on a lightly floured baking sheet.
Bake the flatbreads for 15-20 minutes, or until they are golden brown and crispy.
Remove the flatbreads from the oven, sprinkle with sea salt, and let cool for 5 minutes before serving.
